transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a supply-chain finance facility on the table today -- $6,000,000 in supplier invoices from our approved purchasing division. The preliminary proposal assumes we'd finance 90% of eligible invoices, with ordinary supplier recourse and no special funding or screening controls. Before I make a decision on whether this facility may launch and on what terms, I'd like to conduct our standard round-robin review. I'd like to hear from credit risk, legal, and finance operations in turn. Who would like to begin?

The test confirmed two things: first, funding can only be released twice weekly, not on demand; and second, every invoice requires a 3-business-day hold for duplicate-invoice screening before it can be funded. These constraints conflict with the preliminary proposal's assumption of no special funding or screening controls, and I have not yet recorded these results in the launch checklist. I think it's critical the committee is aware of these operational requirements before any decision is made on whether this facility may launch and on what terms.

transcript.text: Mara, here are the specific findings from the obligor-concentration assessment I received this morning. The single-obligor limit leaves exactly $4,000,000 of the $6,000,000 invoice pool eligible for financing. Additionally, the approved advance rate for that eligible exposure is exactly 85%, not the 90% assumed in the preliminary proposal. This assessment has not yet been uploaded to the credit file, but credit risk recommends that any facility terms reflect an eligible pool of $4,000,000 and an 85% advance rate. These two figures, combined with Nadia's non-recourse requirement and Jon's funding and screening constraints, should all be incorporated into your decision on whether this facility may launch and on what terms.
